title: What if LLMs Ate Their Words: Causal History Effects in Multi-Turn Interaction
abstract: arXiv:2609.05882v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-turn interaction creates a feedback process in which an LLM's previous responses become context for later behavior. Prior work shows substantial multi-turn degradation and that assistant-generated history can affect later behavior. However, it remains unclear how these effects manifest across models, tasks, turns, and inside a model. We study these gaps across six task families and five models. Degradation from fully specified single-turn input (FULL) to progressively revealed multi-turn interaction (SHARDED) is clearly task- and model-dependent, and stronger one-shot performance does not imply greater interaction robustness. We then retrospectively analyze completed SHARDED conversations by replaying the user messages already observed in each trajectory while editing only assistant-generated history. Replacing prior assistant responses with neutral content (termed neutralization) changes downstream min-max normalized performance

translated_title: 如果大语言模型吃掉了自己的话：多轮交互中的因果历史效应
translated_abstract: 多轮交互创造了一个反馈过程，其中大语言模型（LLM）先前的响应会成为后续行为的上下文。先前的研究已表明存在显著的多轮性能退化现象，并且助手生成的历史内容会影响其后续行为。然而，这些效应如何在不同模型、任务、轮次之间以及模型内部表现出来仍不清楚。我们在六个任务族和五个模型上研究了这些空白。从完整指定的单轮输入（FULL）到逐步揭示信息的多轮交互（SHARDED）的性能退化明显依赖于任务和模型，且更强的一次性性能并不意味着更强的交互鲁棒性。随后，我们通过重放每个对话轨迹中已经观察到的用户消息、仅编辑助手生成的历史内容，对已完成的SHARDED对话进行了回顾性分析。用中性内容替换先前的助手响应（称为“中性化”）会改变下游的最小-最大归一化性能。
tldr: 本文研究了多轮交互中LLM自身历史响应对后续行为的因果影响，发现性能退化因任务和模型而异、一次性强性能不等于交互鲁棒性，并通过“中性化”编辑实验证明修改助手历史内容可以直接改变下游任务表现。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates the causal effects of LLMs' own prior responses on their subsequent behavior in multi-turn interactions, finding that degradation is task- and model-dependent, that strong one-shot performance does not guarantee interaction robustness, and that "neutralization" experiments editing assistant-generated history directly change downstream performance.
